lines.text: vi.Springs:Springs arenaturallyoccurring freshwatersourcesfound in thoseplaces where the
water table is located closeto the earth's surface.They obtain theirwater eitherfromaquifers
or from underground streams. Springs located in regions of volcanoes have hot water, while
springs found in area where no volcanic activitytakesplace produce coldwater.
vii. Ponds: Ponds are surface water sources that are mostly smaller than lakes. Some ponds
occur naturally while others are man-made. The main source of water for naturally occurring
ponds is rainfall. Pond water is often used forirrigation, fishing and landscaping.
What'sthe difference between rain, sleetand snow?
When the air is sufficiently saturated,water vapour begins to form clouds. If saturation continues,
vater droplets grow and merge to fall as rain. Snow forms when the air is cold enough to freeze
